newsitem.title: CANADA: CWB sells near 600,000T durum to Iran, buoys price.
newsitem.headline: CWB sells near 600,000T durum to Iran, buoys price.

text.p: A Canadian Wheat Board sale of almost 600,000 tonnes of durum wheat this year to Iran was a first-ever for the CWB and has underpinned durum prices when values on other types of wheat have fallen, CWB chief commissioner Lorne Hehn said.
"The Iranian durum sale is very significant because we've never sold to them before, nor has anyone else," Hehn said.
Canadian analysts at the start of the 1996/97 (Aug/July) marketing year forecast durum prices to slide because of larger North African and European durum wheat crops.
"The Wheat Board shipped half a million tonnes to Iran since July and there's a couple of vessels left," Hehn said.

"It's going to be close to 600,000 tonnes going into that country (Iran). It's done a lot to hold that (durum) wheat price structure up," Hehn said after a speech to United Grain Growers Ltd shareholders here on Thursday.
While the CWB revised its milling wheat prices down C$10 to C$16 a tonne on Oct 24 it left durum wheat prices unchanged at C$205 to C$235 a tonne, FOB Vancouver and St. Lawrence.
The CWB supplies two-thirds world durum market, he said.
Algeria was the CWB's top durum buyer in 1995/96 (Aug/July), buying 1.13 million tonnes, followed by Libya at 970,000 tonnes, CWB documents show.
Algeria was expected to stay the CWB's top durum buyer in 1996/97 but Iran's arrival on the world market was expected to propel it to the second spot as a CWB client, Hehn said.
"We sold to 11 Latin American countries last year and we hope to add Colombia this year," he said.
A potential negative factor on Canadian durum prices may be protein levels that were below customer needs, he added.
"Harvest samples tested by the Canadian Grain Commission indicate an average protein level of about 12 percent. We, and our customers, would prefer to see 13.5 percent," Hehn said.
